editorial.headline: Forage Seed Production Is Nationally Open, but Bali Is Closed
editorial.standfirst: This code covers seed production for livestock feed crops and non-sugar beet, open nationally across all business scales but blocked for foreign registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
This activity is about producing seed, not simply growing feed crops. The scope covers seed propagation for livestock forage plants and non-sugar beet, with the output defined as seed in the form of grain. The work is described as an integrated chain: land preparation, planting, crop care, harvesting, and post-harvest activity carried out as one sequence. In practical terms, it is the upstream agricultural activity that creates planting material for forage systems, rather than the downstream use of those crops as animal feed.

The Indonesian scope is concrete about the kinds of plants involved. Forage crops include grasses and leguminous feed plants, with examples such as elephant grass, king grass, odot grass, setaria grass, alfalfa, kaliandra, gamal, lamtoro, and Indigofera zollingeriana. That gives the code a clear agricultural identity: it sits in the seed-production side of livestock-supporting cultivation, covering both grass-based and legume-based forage seed activity. Non-sugar beet seed production is also included, while the record expressly frames the beet reference as outside sugar beet.

On the national investment reading, the code is open. The record marks PMA status as TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, and the activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar scales. That means the national classification does not, on this slim record, reserve the activity away from foreign investment or limit it to a smaller ownership share. If a founder is looking only at the national PMA column, the immediate signal is therefore simple: this is a foreign-open activity, across the listed business scales, with no foreign-stake cap below full ownership in the provided data.

Bali changes the conclusion completely. The record marks the Bali status as BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO and says the activity is blocked because OSS risk at Besar scale is Rendah or Menengah-Rendah on every scope, triggering the Bali moratorium. The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI used for PMA. So the honest reading is this: nationally, the activity is open to foreign ownership up to 100%; in Bali, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA today under the stated Bali rule. That is not a contradiction in the business scope. It is a location-specific registration block that overrides the practical outcome for Bali planning.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, this is a foreign-open seed-production activity; in Bali, the record’s moratorium makes the practical answer no for PMA registration today.
